deep.reconstruction:
Context. Bundle R.Minimal holds Riemann's material on minimal surfaces with prescribed boundary (published posthumously in 1867 by Hattendorff as 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'). This folio continues a worked example: a minimal surface spanning a polygonal boundary built from straight pieces. The relevant quantities are two sides of given lengths a and b and a further length k. My reading is that k is the separation in the X direction (the X integral is normalised so that X changes by k). The surface is parametrised by an auxiliary variable s, with elliptic differential dw = ds/sqrt((1-s^2)(1-kappa^2 s^2)), modulus kappa. eta is the Gauss-map (stereographic normal) variable, and eta_0, eta_1 are its values at boundary vertices. The handwriting and the editorial margin notes ('streichen!') suggest this may be an elaboration (Hattendorff's?) of Riemann's material rather than a raw Riemann draft; I am unsure.

(1) Parameter ranges. The deleted top lines and the marginal replacement say the following. From the previous page there are two relations, (1-m)^2/(1+m)^2 * ((1-k)/(1+k))^(2k)-type equation and n^2 = k m (m+2k)/(2m+k), where k is the modulus there. Eliminating n leaves one relation between k and m. The previous page showed, by a sign change plus a single-maximum argument, that for every m < 1 this relation has exactly one root k in (0, m). Margin conclusion: for every m < 1 there is exactly one k and one n with 0 < k < n < m < 1. At the endpoints m -> 0 and m -> 1 one has k = n = m [at k = m the n-relation gives n^2 = m^2; at m = 1 the previous page's difference m(1-m^2)^3/((1+3m^2)^2(3+m^2)^2) vanishes]. The earlier deleted text had stated an extra restriction m < m' = 0.1207...; the author abandoned it.

(2) Coordinates, Weierstrass-type representation with additive constants dropped:
  X = (k/K) ∫_1^s dw,
  Y = (k/K) ∫_1^s (eta - 1/eta) dw,
  Z = -(i k/K) ∫_1^s (eta + 1/eta) dw.
The original denominator '2K' was corrected to 'K'; the margin orders all the factors 2 struck. K is presumably the complete elliptic integral of modulus kappa, which normalises the X extent to k. This is the standard pattern dX : dY : dZ = 2 : (eta - 1/eta) : -i(eta + 1/eta) times a common factor, i.e. the Enneper–Weierstrass formulas in Riemann's eta notation.

(3) Side lengths. The two remaining constants are m and sqrt(eta_0 eta_1). They are fixed by the given side lengths a and b:
  a = (i k/K) ∫_1^{1/m} (eta + 1/eta) dw,
  b = (i k/K) ∫_1^{1/m} (eta/sqrt(eta_0 eta_1) + sqrt(eta_0 eta_1)/eta) dw.
On 1 < s < 1/m < 1/kappa the radicand (1-s^2)(1-kappa^2 s^2) is negative, so dw is imaginary and the factor i makes a and b real. This consistency check is mine.

(4) Symmetric case a = b. Take sqrt(eta_0 eta_1) = 1. Then m is determined by one transcendental equation:
  a/k = (i/K) ∫_1^{1/m} (eta + 1/eta) dw =: F(m).

(5) Existence argument. As m runs from 0 to 1, F stays positive and tends to infinity at both ends. Hence F has a minimum at some interior m. So a/k has a lower bound below which the problem has no solution. The next page adds that above the bound there are two values of m, hence two solutions, and conjectures that only the smaller m gives a genuine minimum. This is the analogue of the catenoid/Goldschmidt phenomenon: two critical surfaces, one stable, which disappear below a critical aspect ratio.
errors: The claim that F(m) -> infinity at both ends m -> 0 and m -> 1 is asserted without proof; it is plausible because the endpoints are degenerate (kappa = n = m, where the elliptic integral degenerates), but not shown on the page.

The next-page conclusion 'exactly two values of m for each a/k above the bound' needs F to have a single minimum (unimodality). Only the existence of a minimum is argued, so 'two' is unjustified; 'at least two' (generically, an even number) follows.
The statement that only the smaller m gives a true area minimum is explicitly a conjecture ('Es ist anzunehmen'), not proved.

The normalising factor 2 in the denominators was first written and then struck (margin: 'streichen!'). The correct factor depends on whether X is normalised by K or 2K; this cannot be verified from this page alone.

Several deleted passages (the earlier restriction m < 0.1207 and the deleted limit statement) were superseded; the author correctly abandoned the erroneous bound in favour of the margin argument that every m < 1 works.

results.what: For each m in (0,1) the auxiliary moduli satisfy 0 < k < n < m < 1, with k = n = m in the limits m = 0 and m = 1
results.modern_name: parameter analysis for a Schwarz–Christoffel/Weierstrass representation of a polygon-bounded minimal surface
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous 1867, ed. Hattendorff); Schwarz and Weierstrass for the skew-quadrilateral problems (1865–66)

results.what: Coordinates of the minimal surface as elliptic integrals with factors (eta - 1/eta) and (eta + 1/eta)
results.modern_name: Enneper–Weierstrass representation, with the Gauss map eta as variable

results.what: Side lengths a, b expressed as elliptic-type integrals from s = 1 to s = 1/m; the equal-sides case reduces to a single transcendental equation for m
results.modern_name: period/side-length conditions (solving the period problem) for a Plateau polygon

results.what: a/k has a positive lower bound (no solution below it); above it there are two solutions, only the smaller m conjecturally minimising
results.modern_name: non-existence and bifurcation (fold) of minimal surfaces, analogous to the Goldschmidt/catenoid two-solution phenomenon; stability of only one branch
results.usually_credited_to: catenoid case known since Goldschmidt 1831; analogous discussion appears in Riemann's posthumous minimal-surface memoir (Hattendorff 1867)

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of the worked examples underlying Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface memoir (edited by Hattendorff), so the method is known as his. The qualitative existence threshold plus two-branch/stability remark is a nice detail, but it parallels the classical catenoid picture and probably appears in the published version.

checkable.asserts: At k = m the relation n^2 = k m (m+2k)/(2m+k) gives n = m, consistent with k = n = m at the limit.
The previous page's difference at k = m vanishes at m = 1 (returns 0), so k = m is the root at m = 1, consistent with k = n = m there.

∫_1^{1/kappa} ds/sqrt((1-s^2)(1-kappa^2 s^2)) = ∓ i K'(kappa) (purely imaginary), so the factor i in the formulas for a, b, Z yields real lengths. The overall sign depends on the branch of the square root.
For kappa < m and 1 < s < 1/m the radicand is negative (here -0.94), confirming the integrand is imaginary on the integration path of a and b.

transcription_corrections: '0 < [-κ < κ < m < m-]' should read '0 < k < n < m < 1' (deleted in the text, restated in the margin as 0 < κ < n < m < 1). The transcription conflates the moduli k/κ with n.
'κ = κ = m' should be 'κ (=k) = n = m', and 'm = [-m-]1' should read m = 1.
The prefactor denominator read as 'κ' is most likely a capital K (complete elliptic integral), i.e. k/K, with an originally written factor 2 struck out (margin: '2 2 2 } streichen!').
'von 0 bis 1/[-m-]' should read 'von 0 bis 1' (m runs from 0 to 1).
In the margin, 'einen Werth von κ und einen Werth von κ' should be 'einen Werth von κ und einen Werth von n'.
In the deleted top passage, 'zu jedem Werthe von m einen Werth von κ und von n'.
